scenes.heading: Graphs of parabolas
scenes.say: Throw a basketball and its path makes a smooth curve called a parabola. Today you will plot parabolas and learn to read their key features.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A half-pipe dips to one low point with matching sides
scenes.science: A parabola has one turning point and mirror-image sides
scenes.breaks: A half-pipe stops at the top, but a parabola keeps going up forever.
scenes.say: Picture a skate half-pipe. It dips down to one lowest point, and the two sides are perfect mirror images. A parabola is the same: one turning point and two matching sides. The difference is that a parabola never stops; it keeps rising forever.

scenes.heading: The features of a parabola
scenes.say: Here is y equals x squared minus two x minus three. First the curve, then its features. The lowest point, one, negative four, is the turning point. The dashed line x equals one is the axis of symmetry. It crosses the x-axis at negative one and three, and the y-axis at negative three.
scenes.caption: y = x² − 2x − 3. Turning point (1, −4). Axis of symmetry x = 1. x-intercepts −1 and 3, y-intercept −3.

scenes.heading: Smile or frown?
scenes.say: Look at the number in front of x squared. If it is positive, the parabola smiles: it opens upwards and has a minimum. If it is negative, it frowns: it opens downwards and has a maximum.

scenes.heading: Turning point from intercepts
scenes.question: y = x² + 4x − 5 has x-intercepts −5 and 1. Find the turning point.
scenes.say: The axis of symmetry is halfway between the x-intercepts. Negative five plus one is negative four; halve it to get negative two. Substitute negative two into the rule: four minus eight minus five is negative nine. So the turning point is negative two, negative nine.
scenes.caption: The axis is halfway between the x-intercepts: (−5 + 1) ÷ 2 = −2. Substitute: 4 − 8 − 5 = −9. Turning point (−2, −9).

points: y = ax² + bx + c makes a parabola
a positive: minimum; a negative: maximum
Axis of symmetry: x = a number
scenes.say: Quick recap. Quadratic rules make parabolas. Positive smiles with a minimum, negative frowns with a maximum. The axis of symmetry is a vertical line, halfway between the x-intercepts. And the y-intercept is the constant c. Now try the practice questions!
